name: Genesis

objectives.text: Identify Genesis as the first book of the Bible and the book that tells how the world began
Recall that God made everything out of nothing and called what he made good
Retell in order what God made on each of the six days of creation and his rest on the seventh day
Name Adam and Eve as the first man and woman and explain that God made them in his image
Retell the account of Adam and Eve's disobedience in the garden and the consequences God announced
Retell the account of Noah, the ark, and the flood, including God's rainbow promise
Describe how sin spread after the fall through the accounts of Cain and Abel and the tower of Babel
Summarize the main events in the lives of Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and Joseph
Describe the work God gave humans in the garden and the purpose of the seventh day rest
Explain the two main sections of Genesis, the primeval history of chapters 1 to 11 and the patriarchal history of chapters 12 to 50
Explain the promises God made to Abraham of land, descendants, and blessing to all nations
Explain what Genesis 2 teaches about marriage as God's design for one man and one woman
Compare the condition of humanity at creation with its condition after the fall
Explain how Abraham was counted righteous by believing God's promise and how the New Testament uses this text
Explain how the beginnings recorded in Genesis lay the foundation for themes developed in the rest of the Bible
Analyze how the repeated toledot heading, these are the generations of, organizes the book of Genesis
Interpret the testing of Abraham with Isaac in light of its New Testament interpretation
Trace the promise of the seed of the woman through the family lines of Genesis to the promised ruler from Judah
Explain the significance of the Abrahamic covenant and its sign of circumcision as the Reformed tradition understands the covenant of grace
Compare the covenant God made with Noah to the covenant he made with Abraham
Explain the Reformed doctrine of election as illustrated in God's choice of Jacob over Esau
Analyze how Genesis portrays the patriarchs as flawed people through whom God keeps his promises
Explain the theological significance of the image of God in Genesis for human dignity
Evaluate arguments for and against Mosaic authorship of Genesis, including the Documentary Hypothesis
Contrast the theology of Genesis 1 to 11 with ancient Near Eastern creation and flood accounts
Evaluate major interpretive views of the creation days in Genesis 1, including the literal six day view and the framework view, using principles of interpreting Scripture by Scripture
Research the cultural background of patriarchal customs and explain how it illuminates passages in Genesis
Explain how Genesis teaches the Reformed doctrine of original sin and its transmission from Adam to all humanity
Synthesize the theme of God's providence in the Joseph narrative into a written argument drawing on the text and the confessions

changes: Kept and reworded real competencies (book of beginnings, Adam and Eve, Noah, patriarchs, two sections, toledot, Abrahamic covenant, seed of the woman, election, Mosaic authorship, creation views, cultural background, Joseph and providence). Replaced vague items (observe God made everything good, categorize Genesis as foundation, compare creation with fall) with assessable versions. Added creation days, spread of sin, work and Sabbath, marriage, justification by faith, testing of Abraham, Noahic covenant, flawed patriarchs, image of God, ancient Near Eastern comparison, and original sin. Corrected confession citations to full names and added specific verse anchors.
